sentences.text: Shri Teekaram Tantuvay- Advocate for applicant.

Shri Arvind Singh- Government Advocate for respondent/Stat
 Order

This is repeat (second) application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (new Section 483 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.136/2024 registered at Police Station Budhni, District Sehore (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 386, 420, 392 and 34 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Earlier application filed by applicant was dismissed as withdrawn.
3. Learned counsel appearing for applicant submitted that applicant is in jail since 12.04.2024.
It is further submitted that complainant has been examined and he is hostile.
Applicant is innocent and falsely been implicated.
He is in jail for sometime.
In these circumstances, applicant be released on bail.
4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for State opposed the prayer but could not deny the position that complainant has turned hostile in Court.
It is further submitted that applicant is having ten cases of similar in nature.
Earlier offences committed are serious in nature.
In these circumstances, applicant may not be released on bail.
5. Heard the counsel for the parties.

sentences.text:
Considering the fact that applicant is in jail since 12.04.2024, trial is likely to take long time,
complainant has been examined and he is hostile, bail application filed by applicant is allowed with following conditions :-
(i) Applicant will mark his presence before local police station twice every month till completion of trial and will furnish FDR of Rs. 1,00,000/- before the trial Court.
(ii) Applicant will not involve himself in any other offence in future.
(iii) If applicant is found involved in any other offence in future, then the FDR will be forfeited in favour of State Government.
(iv) Applicant will not threaten the witnesses of the case or will influence them by approaching himself or through his agent.
(v) No unnecessary adjournment shall be taken by applicant before trial Court.
(vi) Trial Court shall conclude the trial expeditiously and may not give unnecessary adjournment to applicant.

7. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on aforesaid conditions on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial.
